scams.name: Fortaleza (FOR) Airport Taxi Mafia & Uber Pickup-Zone Confusion
scams.description:
Fortaleza International Airport (Aeroporto Pinto Martins, IATA FOR) sits 6 km south of Centro and 10 km south of the Beira Mar / Meireles tourist corridor, and the arrivals hall hosts a documented 2025 overcharge ecosystem.

Legitimate cost in 2026: Uber / 99 / Cabify from FOR to Beira Mar / Meireles is R$25–R$45 (15–20 min via Av. Washington Soares); to Centro R$20–R$35; to Praia do Futuro R$30–R$50; to Cumbuco (40 km NW) R$90–R$140 (45 min). Budget public option: the Ônibus 066 'Aeroporto–Benfica' links FOR to Centro at R$5.00 per person (45 min). Scam patterns: (a) 'Special Taxi' / 'Taxi Vermelho' kiosks INSIDE the terminal quote R$100–R$250 flat to Meireles — real cost R$25–R$45 via app; (b) curbside taxi drivers at the arrivals gate demand 'cash only R$150' with no meter; (c) 'meter broken — R$180 fixed to your hotel' after pulling out of the airport; (d) fake airport rideshare pickup-zone signs directing tourists AWAY from the real 'Aplicativos' zone (signposted on the second level at Terminal 2); (e) some FOR drivers refuse the app-quoted price on arrival and demand a cash top-up R$50–R$100 — cancel the trip in-app + rebook with another driver; (f) late-night (after 11 PM) Uber wait times spike to 15–25 min — unlicensed 'mototaxis' and predatory street taxis fill the gap.

For travelers: (1) book Uber / 99 / Cabify on airport Wi-Fi AFTER luggage; (2) meet the driver at the designated 'Aplicativos' pickup zone on the second level at Terminal 2 (follow 'Aplicativos' signs, NOT 'Taxi' kiosks); (3) for late-night arrivals (after 11 PM), pre-book a transfer via your hotel or Carioca Transfers / Fortaleza Transfer at R$80–R$150 fixed — worth it to avoid app-wait-time frustration; (4) Ignore every 'Special Taxi' kiosk inside the terminal quoting R$100+ to Meireles — those are the overcharge operation; (5) Don't hand a credit card to any taxi driver; ONLY pay via the Uber / 99 in-app card or cash against the meter if using a registered 'Taxi Comum' from the official rank; (6) for return to FOR, pre-book Uber the night before — saves time at hotel pickup; (7) if a driver demands cash on top of the in-app price, refuse politely, exit the vehicle, cancel the trip in-app + report via the in-app safety button; (8) DEATUR Fortaleza +55 85 3101 2488 (Tourist Police, English available); Polícia Militar 190, SAMU 192. Book Uber, 99, or Cabify on airport Wi-Fi AFTER your luggage — typical FOR-Meireles R$25–R$45, FOR-Centro R$20–R$35, FOR-Praia do Futuro R$30–R$50. Meet driver at the signposted "Aplicativos" zone on Terminal 2's second level. IGNORE every "Special Taxi" or "Taxi Vermelho" kiosk inside the terminal quoting R$100+. For late-night arrivals after 11 PM, pre-book Carioca Transfers or Fortaleza Transfer at R$80–R$150 fixed. Refuse every "cash top-up" demand from Uber drivers — cancel in-app and use the safety button. Save DEATUR Fortaleza +55 85 3101 2488.
scams.avoidance: Book Uber / 99 / Cabify on airport Wi-Fi AFTER luggage (FOR-Meireles R$25–R$45; FOR-Centro R$20–R$35) Meet driver at 'Aplicativos' pickup zone on Terminal 2 second level (signposted) For late-night arrivals, pre-book Carioca Transfers / Fortaleza Transfer R$80–R$150 fixed IGNORE every 'Special Taxi' kiosk inside terminal; NEVER hand credit card to taxi driver DEATUR Fortaleza +55 85 3101 2488; Polícia Militar 190; SAMU 192
scams.location: Aeroporto Pinto Martins (FOR), arrivals hall, rideshare pickup zone
scams.tldr: Fortaleza Airport (FOR) "Special Taxi" / "Taxi Vermelho" kiosks quote R$100–R$250 to Beira Mar/Meireles (real Uber R$25–R$45); curbside drivers demand "cash only R$150" with no meter; and Uber drivers run "cash top-up" scams demanding R$50–R$100 above the in-app price.

scams.name: Terminal da Parangaba Walkway Distraction-Pickpocket Scam
scams.description:
Terminal da Parangaba is a major bus and metro interchange in northern Fortaleza (Metrô Linha Sul terminus, plus inter-city bus routes to Beira Mar, Centro, and the western coastal zones). The elevated pedestrian walkway ('passarela') connecting the metro station to the bus terminal is a documented 2025 pickpocket and distraction-scam hot-spot. Traveler-community reports describe coordinated teams using turnstile distractions to lift wallets and phones during the 10-second chokepoint, plus adjacent rideshare-scam pressure on visibly disoriented tourists.

The 2025 scam patterns: (a) a 'helper' offering to swipe your metro card through the turnstile 'because yours isn't working' — while the accomplice picks your pocket during the fumble; (b) a staged 'fall' or 'medical emergency' in the walkway chokepoint — bystanders gather, your bag is lifted; (c) the 'spill' — someone bumps you with a drink / spilled yoghurt, a second person 'helps clean you up' while lifting your phone from your pocket or bag; (d) the 'dropped-coin' distraction — someone drops coins at your feet, you look down, the team lifts from your back pocket; (e) phone-snatch-and-run — motorbike rider on the walkway's surface-level end reaches up and grabs a phone held in view; (f) aggressive 'metro ticket seller' approach with distracting sales pitch while accomplice rifles an open tote or backpack front pocket. The walkway is particularly dangerous during peak hours (7–9 AM, 5–7 PM) and after 8 PM when foot-traffic thins and police presence drops.

For travelers: (1) Avoid Terminal da Parangaba for tourist transit — it is a local commuter hub, not a tourist route; use Uber / 99 from Beira Mar / Meireles directly to your destination; (2) IF you must use the metro, enter / exit via Metrô Linha Sul at Benfica or Chico da Silva stations (Centro-facing), NOT Parangaba; (3) carry ONLY a decoy phone + R$100 cash in a front pocket; leave passport, credit cards, and primary phone in the hotel safe; (4) Refuse every 'helper' approach at turnstiles — say 'não preciso' firmly and walk past; (5) use a CROSS-BODY bag worn in FRONT (not backpack on back) at any transit terminal; (6) if bumped or spilled on, IMMEDIATELY grab your bag + phone before responding to the 'helper' — the 'help' IS the scam; (7) if phone-snatched by motorbike, Don't chase — Fortaleza snatch-rings are often armed; report via DEATUR +55 85 3101 2488 and Polícia Militar 190 within 24 hours for the police report needed for travel insurance; (8) for cheap cross-city travel, use Uber / 99 R$15–R$35 within Fortaleza — MUCH safer than Terminal da Parangaba for any traveler. AVOID Terminal da Parangaba for tourist transit entirely — it's a local commuter hub; use Uber or 99 from Beira Mar / Meireles directly to your destination at R$15–R$35 within Fortaleza. Carry ONLY a decoy phone + R$100 cash in a front pocket; passport and primary credit cards stay in the hotel safe. Wear a CROSS-BODY bag in FRONT (never a backpack on your back) at any transit terminal. Refuse every "metro card helper" approach with a firm "não preciso." If bumped or spilled on, IMMEDIATELY grab your bag and phone before responding to any "helper" — the help IS the scam.
scams.avoidance: AVOID Terminal da Parangaba for tourist transit — use Uber / 99 direct from Meireles Carry decoy phone + R$100 cash ONLY; passport + cards in hotel safe Cross-body bag worn in FRONT at any transit terminal; REFUSE every 'helper' approach If bumped or spilled on, grab bag + phone FIRST before responding to 'helper' DEATUR Fortaleza +55 85 3101 2488; Polícia Militar 190; file report within 24 hr for insurance
scams.location: Terminal da Parangaba bus / metro station walkway, northern Fortaleza
scams.tldr: Terminal da Parangaba's elevated walkway hosts coordinated 2025 distraction-pickpocket teams — "metro card helpers" at turnstiles, staged "spills" with fake-clean-up assists, and motorbike phone-snatch at the surface-level walkway end target older travelers in the 10-second chokepoint.

scams.name: Beira Mar / Praia de Iracema Pickpocket & Phone-Snatch Ring
scams.description:
The Av. Beira Mar orla (3-km beachfront promenade running from Praia do Mucuripe through Meireles to Praia de Iracema) is Fortaleza's primary tourist corridor — boutique hotels, restaurants, beach kiosks, and the nightly Feira de Artesanato craft market. It is also a documented 2025 phone-snatch and pickpocket hot-spot, particularly after sunset.

The 2025 scam patterns: (a) motorbike phone-snatch on the Beira Mar cycle path — rider pulls alongside, grabs phone from tourist holding it for a photo; (b) 'tourist tip' scam at beach kiosks — a vendor offers to 'watch your bag while you swim', then disappears with it; (c) the Praia de Iracema Ponte Metálica 'photo helper' — someone offers to take your photo at the iconic bridge, then runs with the phone; (d) aggressive vendor pressure at Feira de Artesanato (nightly Beira Mar craft market, 6 PM–11 PM) — vendor blocks your path while accomplice rifles an open bag; (e) Praia de Iracema nightlife strip (Dragão do Mar + Mucuripe Club area) drink-spike + wallet-lift pattern, particularly targeting solo female travelers; (f) 'beach boy' approaches offering sunset-beach tours / caipirinhas who later demand R$200+ for 'my time'; (g) hotel-to-restaurant walks at night after 9 PM — tourists carrying phones visibly are targeted; (h) Praia do Futuro barraca (beach kiosks) credit-card cloning — insist on seeing the card machine + keep card in sight.

For travelers: (1) Don't hold your phone visibly while walking the Beira Mar orla or cycle path — especially close to the street; use a cross-body bag worn in FRONT and take photos quickly then stow immediately; (2) Don't leave bags or valuables unattended on the beach — use beach locker at reputable hotels (Gran Marquise, Praiano Hotel, Luzeiros) or leave at hotel and bring decoy phone + R$100 only; (3) Refuse every 'photo helper' approach at Ponte Metálica — use a selfie stick or ask a uniformed police officer for assistance; (4) at Feira de Artesanato, keep bags zipped + worn in front; pay with cash in small bills — decline to pull out large R$ notes; (5) Avoid the Praia de Iracema nightlife strip for solo female travelers after 10 PM — use Uber for restaurant-to-hotel; (6) at Praia do Futuro barracas, pay in cash where possible; if using card, insist on seeing the card machine at all times; reputable barracas: Chico do Caranguejo, Itapariká, Crocobeach; (7) for travelers, the safer evening alternative to Beira Mar orla walking is the enclosed Shopping Iguatemi or Shopping RioMar (malls with 24/7 security, cinemas, restaurants); (8) DEATUR Fortaleza +55 85 3101 2488; Polícia Militar 190; file police report within 24 hr for travel insurance. Don't hold your phone visibly while walking the Beira Mar orla cycle path — use a cross-body bag in FRONT, take photos quickly, then stow immediately. Never leave bags or valuables unattended on the beach (use hotel locker or carry decoy phone + R$100 only). Refuse every "photo helper" approach at Ponte Metálica and aggressive vendor pressure at Feira de Artesanato. AVOID Praia de Iracema nightlife strip after 10 PM for solo female travelers — Uber from restaurant to hotel. At Praia do Futuro barracas, keep your card in sight at all times during payment; reputable: Chico do Caranguejo, Itapariká, Crocobeach.
scams.avoidance: Cross-body bag worn in FRONT on Beira Mar orla; phone stowed when walking NEVER leave valuables on beach; use hotel locker or decoy phone + R$100 only REFUSE every 'photo helper' approach — use selfie stick or uniformed police At Feira de Artesanato pay in small cash bills; AVOID Praia de Iracema nightlife strip after 10 PM DEATUR Fortaleza +55 85 3101 2488; Polícia Militar 190; SAMU 192
scams.location: Av. Beira Mar orla, Praia de Iracema, Meireles beachfront promenade
scams.tldr: Motorbike phone-snatch crews work the Av. Beira Mar cycle path and Praia de Iracema after sunset; Feira de Artesanato vendors run "free photo helper" runs at Ponte Metálica and bag-rifle distractions; "beach boy" caipirinha hosts later demand R$200+ "for my time"; and Praia do Futuro barracas run credit-card cloning if cards leave your sight.

scams.name: Jericoacoara & Canoa Quebrada Buggy Day-Trip Overcharge & Commission Scam
scams.description:
Jericoacoara (300 km NW, 5–6 hour drive through Ceará's coastal sand-roads) and Canoa Quebrada (160 km SE, 2.5-hour drive) are Ceará's flagship beach excursions from Fortaleza — and 2025 hotel concierges plus Beira Mar tour-desk touts host a commission-markup ecosystem layered on top of legitimate operator pricing.

Legitimate 2026 cost: Canoa Quebrada day-trip group bus R$120–R$180 per person via Fretur / Litoral Tours / Tour Shop (departs Beira Mar 7 AM, returns 6 PM, includes buggy ride R$80 on-site); Canoa Quebrada self-drive with rental car R$180–R$280 per day. Jericoacoara is BETTER as 2–3 day overnight (not day-trip — the drive is 5–6 hours one way): group bus overnight from Fortaleza R$350–R$550 per person via Jeri Off Road / Top Buggy; alternatively fly FOR-JJD (Jericoacoara airport) via Azul at R$400–R$700 round-trip (1 hour). Local buggy ride on Jeri R$120–R$200 (4 passengers split) for Lagoa do Paraíso + Lagoa Azul + Pedra Furada circuit. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) hotel concierge 'VIP private buggy Canoa day-trip R$1,200' (real group R$120–R$180); (b) airport tour-desk 'Jericoacoara same-day helicopter tour R$3,500' (real fly-and-return Azul R$400–R$700 if you must do it in a day); (c) Beira Mar tout selling 'Jeri 2-day all-inclusive R$2,200' with undisclosed commission stops (real R$600–R$900 with reputable operator); (d) unlicensed buggy drivers on Jeri offering 'circuito completo R$500' (real R$120–R$200 via cooperative at Pousada's desk); (e) 'mandatory environmental tax R$100' demanded at Jericoacoara park entrance (real R$10 Parque Nacional de Jericoacoara entry); (f) Canoa Quebrada buggy 'emoção forte / adrenaline option R$150' added surprise at the end of ride (fair is R$80 fixed); (g) 'Lagoa do Paraíso private table R$300' demand at the lagoon hammock restaurants (tables are free with food order).

For travelers: (1) Canoa Quebrada is feasible as a 1-day trip — book group bus via Fretur / Litoral Tours / Tour Shop R$120–R$180 per person, confirm itinerary in writing (Beira Mar 7 AM departure, return 6 PM, includes buggy ride) — Refuse every hotel-concierge 'VIP private R$1,200' upsell; (2) Jericoacoara is BEST as 2–3 night overnight — drive is 5–6 hours each way, same-day is rushed and punishing; fly FOR-JJD via Azul R$400–R$700 round-trip OR book overnight bus R$350–R$550 via Jeri Off Road / Top Buggy; (3) on Jeri, book the local buggy cooperative DIRECT via your pousada's desk at R$120–R$200 (4-pax split) for the Lagoa do Paraíso / Lagoa Azul / Pedra Furada circuit — Refuse every 'circuito completo R$500' unlicensed driver; (4) Parque Nacional de Jericoacoara entry is R$10 (federal park fee) — Refuse every 'mandatory environmental tax R$100' demand at the gate; ask for receipt; (5) at Lagoa do Paraíso, the iconic hammock tables over the water are free with food order at Hammock Restaurant / Paraíso Restaurant — Refuse every 'private table R$300' demand; (6) Canoa Quebrada buggy: confirm fixed price R$80 BEFORE boarding, Refuse 'adrenaline option R$150' surprise add-on; (7) reputable Jeri pousadas: Vila Kalango, Tatajuba Beach, Essenza Hotel, Pousada Jeri; reputable Canoa pousadas: Pousada Califórnia, Lua Morena; (8) for travelers, if Jeri's 5-hour sandy-road drive is daunting, fly Azul FOR-JJD — lands directly in Jericoacoara at the small Jeri airport; (9) DEATUR Fortaleza +55 85 3101 2488; Polícia Militar 190. For Canoa Quebrada day-trip, book a group bus via Fretur, Litoral Tours, or Tour Shop at R$120–R$180 per person — confirm itinerary in writing (Beira Mar 7 AM departure, return 6 PM). For Jericoacoara, plan a 2–3 night overnight (5–6 hour drive each way is too punishing as a day-trip) — book the bus R$350–R$550 via Jeri Off Road / Top Buggy OR fly Azul FOR-JJD round-trip R$400–R$700. On Jeri, book the buggy cooperative DIRECT via your pousada at R$120–R$200 (4-pax split) and refuse "circuito completo R$500" unlicensed offers. Parque Nacional de Jericoacoara entry is R$10 — refuse "mandatory environmental tax R$100" demands.
scams.avoidance: Canoa Quebrada: group day-trip R$120–R$180 via Fretur / Litoral Tours / Tour Shop Jericoacoara: 2–3 day overnight R$350–R$550 bus OR fly Azul FOR-JJD R$400–R$700 Local Jeri buggy R$120–R$200 (4-pax split) via pousada cooperative; Parque entry R$10 REFUSE every hotel-concierge private upsell above R$800 per person; REFUSE 'mandatory R$100' tax Lagoa do Paraíso hammock tables FREE with food order; REFUSE 'private table R$300'
scams.location: Av. Beira Mar hotel lobbies + Pinto Martins airport tour-desk area
scams.tldr: Beira Mar hotel concierges and tour-desk touts upsell Canoa Quebrada day-trips at R$1,200 "VIP private" (real group R$120–R$180), Jericoacoara "all-inclusive" packages at R$2,200+ with hidden commission stops (real R$600–R$900 reputable), and unlicensed "Jeri circuito completo" buggy at R$500 (real R$120–R$200 cooperative).

scams.name: Beira Mar & Praia do Futuro Restaurant Couvert + Serviço Padding & 'Preço de Mercado' Seafood Trap
scams.description:
Fortaleza's Av. Beira Mar restaurant strip (Meireles to Praia do Mucuripe) and the Praia do Futuro barraca (beach-kiosk) corridor host the standard Brazilian tourist-restaurant overcharge pattern — couvert artístico padding, surprise serviço charges, credit-card surcharges, and the "preço de mercado" (market-price) seafood trap.

Brazilian restaurant law (Lei 13.419/2017) makes the 10% serviço charge OPTIONAL — you can refuse it, particularly for poor service. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) 'couvert artístico R$80–R$150 per person' at Beira Mar restaurants (legitimate R$15–R$35 for a genuine Ceará musician — Forró / Brega music); (b) 'serviço 10%' added silently + photographed menu shows 'serviço opcional' fine print; (c) Praia do Futuro barraca 'camarão ao alho e óleo preço de mercado' with no R$ per kg quoted — bill arrives R$180 for a 300g portion (real R$80–R$120 for same quantity); (d) 'lagosta fresh catch R$350' without clarifying per-kg basis — arrives as 800g serving billed R$850; (e) bottled-water pricing R$20–R$35 at beach barracas (real R$5–R$10); (f) credit-card surcharge 5–10% added only at bill-time ('we prefer PIX'); (g) 'gringo menu' in English with 15–30% markup vs the Portuguese local menu; (h) Feira de Artesanato food-stall skewer / tapioca prices doubling when a gringo orders (local R$8, gringo R$18).

For travelers: (1) BEFORE sitting, ask for the menu (carta) in Portuguese AND confirm in writing: (a) the couvert artístico R$ amount per person, (b) serviço 10% policy — photograph the menu page showing 'serviço opcional' (OPTIONAL under Lei 13.419/2017), (c) credit-card surcharge; (2) for seafood, AGREE weight in R$ per kg IN WRITING BEFORE cooking — fair 2026 Fortaleza lobster R$250–R$450 per kg, camarão rosa R$120–R$200 per kg, peixe do dia (daily catch) R$80–R$140 per kg; (3) at Praia do Futuro barracas, the BEST value are the weekday afternoon 'rodada de caranguejo' crab nights (Quarta-feira at Chico do Caranguejo, R$60–R$100 all-you-can-eat); reputable barracas: Chico do Caranguejo, Itapariká, Crocobeach, Vira Verão; (4) Avoid restaurants with English-only menus posted outside — walk 1–2 blocks inland for authentic local prices; reputable Beira Mar area: Coco Bambu Varjota (Google 4.6+, R$80–R$180), Pulcinella Varjota (Italian, R$70–R$140), Moleskine Gastrobar (R$60–R$120); (5) if serviço is added against your wishes for poor service, politely Refuse and cite Lei 13.419/2017 — the manager knows this; (6) for bottled water, bring your own from hotel / supermarket (R$3–R$5) — skip the beach barraca R$20–R$35 markup; (7) Feira de Artesanato food stalls: pay in Portuguese ('quanto é?') + small bills (R$10, R$20 notes) — vendors who pad prices fold when you present local-tier cash; (8) PROCON Ceará 151 for billing disputes. BEFORE sitting at any Beira Mar restaurant or Praia do Futuro barraca, ask for the menu in Portuguese and confirm in writing: (a) couvert artístico R$ amount per person (legit R$15–R$35), (b) serviço 10% policy (OPTIONAL under Lei 13.419/2017), (c) credit-card surcharge — photograph the menu. For seafood, AGREE weight × R$ per kg in writing BEFORE cooking (lobster R$250–R$450/kg, camarão rosa R$120–R$200/kg, peixe do dia R$80–R$140/kg). Reputable: Coco Bambu Varjota, Pulcinella, Moleskine; barracas Chico do Caranguejo, Itapariká, Crocobeach. Refuse silent serviço (Lei 13.419/2017); PROCON Ceará 151.
scams.avoidance: BEFORE sitting, confirm couvert R$ + serviço policy + card surcharge IN WRITING; photograph menu Seafood: agree R$ per kg BEFORE cooking (lobster R$250–R$450/kg; camarão rosa R$120–R$200/kg) Reputable: Coco Bambu Varjota / Pulcinella / Moleskine; barracas Chico do Caranguejo / Itapariká REFUSE serviço if poor service (Lei 13.419/2017 — OPTIONAL); PROCON Ceará 151 for disputes Bring bottled water from hotel; pay Feira de Artesanato stalls in small R$ bills + Portuguese
scams.location: Av. Beira Mar restaurants, Praia do Futuro barracas, Mucuripe waterfront
scams.tldr: Av. Beira Mar restaurants and Praia do Futuro barracas pad bills with R$80–R$150 "couvert artístico" (legit R$15–R$35), silent 10% serviço (Lei 13.419/2017 makes it OPTIONAL), R$20–R$35 bottled water (real R$5–R$10), and verbal "preço de mercado" seafood quotes that turn 300g shrimp into R$180 surprises.

scams.name: Fortaleza Réveillon & Fortal Carnaval Booking Fraud + Accommodation Cancel-and-Relist
scams.description:
Fortaleza hosts two mega-events that drive nationwide booking-fraud patterns: Réveillon (New Year's Eve, with 2+ million-person fireworks display at Aterro da Praia de Iracema) and Fortal (Brazil's largest out-of-season Carnaval, late July, 4 nights of trio elétrico parades in Cidade Fortal stadium 20 km south of Centro). Both draw Airbnb cancel-and-relist fraud and counterfeit-ticket operations.

The 2025–2026 scam patterns: (a) Airbnb cancel-and-relist — host accepts your booking 6–9 months out at R$400/night, then cancels 30 days before your dates citing 'pipe burst' / 'family emergency' / 'host illness' — re-lists the same unit at R$1,200/night immediately; Airbnb refunds the original payment but you are left scrambling 30 days out with peak-season pricing; (b) Instagram / WhatsApp 'aluguel temporada' sellers demanding PIX-transfer deposit — Brazilian PIX is IRREVERSIBLE, and the listing disappears after payment; (c) counterfeit Fortal camarote / front-row ticket resellers on Facebook Marketplace + WhatsApp groups at 50–70% discount off face value — tickets are fake QR codes that scan 'invalid' at the Cidade Fortal gate; (d) fake 'Fortal abadá block purchase' Instagram accounts selling 4-night R$800 abadás for R$400 — never arrive; (e) Réveillon 'VIP reserved-beach-spot R$500 per person' at Aterro da Praia de Iracema — the Réveillon fireworks viewing area is 100% PUBLIC (federal beach), no reservation legitimately exists; (f) hotel overbooking for Réveillon — properties oversell the peak week then 'relocate' paying guests 10 km inland the night of arrival; (g) 'all-inclusive Fortal package R$3,500 including transport + camarote + hotel' sold via WhatsApp — the package doesn't exist, the seller blocks your number after PIX transfer.

For travelers: (1) BOOK accommodation 9–12 months ahead for Réveillon (Dec 28–Jan 3) and Fortal (late July) via RECOGNIZED hotel chains ONLY — reputable: Gran Marquise Hotel (Meireles), Praiano Hotel, Luzeiros, Hotel Ponta Mar, Mareiro Hotel, Vila Galé Fortaleza; (2) Avoid Airbnb for these dates entirely — cancel-and-relist pattern is well-documented per Brazilian traveler reports; (3) Never PIX-transfer to Instagram / WhatsApp 'aluguel temporada' sellers — the payment is IRREVERSIBLE with no recovery recourse; (4) for Fortal tickets (camarote, abadá, front-row), buy ONLY through the official Fortal website (fortal.com.br) or authorized outlets Ingresso.com / Sympla — skip EVERY Facebook / WhatsApp / Instagram 'discount resale'; (5) the Réveillon fireworks viewing at Aterro da Praia de Iracema is 100% free + PUBLIC — Refuse every 'VIP beach spot R$500' offer; arrive early (by 8 PM) and stake out a spot; (6) confirm your hotel booking 72 hours before arrival via direct phone call (NOT email); if overbooking is mentioned, demand written confirmation of the alternate property + the hotel chain's transfer commitment in writing BEFORE leaving the original reservation; (7) for Fortal, the SAFEST plan is 3-night package from your Meireles hotel with round-trip Cidade Fortal shuttle (R$150 per night round-trip) — skip the 'all-inclusive Fortal WhatsApp package'; (8) PROCON Ceará 151; DEATUR Fortaleza +55 85 3101 2488. Book Réveillon and Fortal accommodation 9–12 months ahead via RECOGNIZED hotel chains only — Gran Marquise (Meireles), Praiano Hotel, Luzeiros, Hotel Ponta Mar, Mareiro, Vila Galé Fortaleza. AVOID Airbnb for these dates entirely (cancel-and-relist documented). Buy Fortal tickets ONLY through fortal.com.br or authorized outlets Ingresso.com / Sympla — refuse every Facebook / WhatsApp / Instagram "discount resale." NEVER PIX-transfer to Instagram or WhatsApp "aluguel temporada" sellers — irreversible. Réveillon Aterro fireworks viewing is FREE and PUBLIC; refuse every "VIP beach spot R$500" offer; arrive by 8 PM to stake out a spot.
scams.avoidance: Book 9–12 mo ahead via hotel chains: Gran Marquise / Praiano / Luzeiros / Ponta Mar / Vila Galé AVOID Airbnb for Réveillon + Fortal; NEVER PIX-transfer to Instagram / WhatsApp sellers Fortal tickets ONLY via fortal.com.br / Ingresso.com / Sympla — skip all resellers Réveillon Aterro fireworks FREE + PUBLIC — arrive 8 PM; refuse every 'VIP spot' offer Confirm hotel 72hr pre-arrival by PHONE; demand written overbooking-relocation terms; PROCON 151
scams.location: Booking platforms, Airbnb / Instagram / WhatsApp 'aluguel temporada' sellers
scams.tldr: Fortaleza Réveillon (Dec 28–Jan 3) and Fortal Carnaval (late July) drive Airbnb cancel-and-relist fraud at 3× original rates 30 days out, irreversible WhatsApp PIX-deposit scams for fake "all-inclusive" packages, counterfeit Fortal camarote ticket QR codes, and "VIP reserved beach spot R$500" demands at the public Aterro fireworks viewing.
